EngLawName: Act on Strengthening National Defense Self-Reliance and Developing Unmanned Systems Industry
name: 強化國防自主暨無人載具產業發展條例
histories: Promulgated by Presidential Order No. Hua-Zong-1-Jing-Zi-11500086651 dated September 11, 2026, with the full text consisting of 24 articles. Pursuant to Article 24, this Act shall enter into force six (6) months after its promulgation, except that Article 4 shall take effect upon promulgation.

articles.content: This Act is enacted to strengthen Taiwan’s national defense self-reliance, to channel the private sector’s outstanding information and communications technology (ICT) and precision machinery capabilities into the industries of national defense and Unmanned Systems, to promote the two-way transfer of dual-use technologies between the military and civilian sectors, and to establish and comply with standards fora Trusted Supply Chain, thereby achieving the dual-objectives of national defense self-reliance and industrial upgrading.

The competent authority of this Act (the “Competent Authority”) shall be the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), except that the Ministry of National Defense (MND) shall be the Competent Authority for matters involving national defense and military procurement.
Matters under this Act involving national defense procurement, subsidies for research and development, imports of critical technologies, cybersecurity reviews, and designation of testing sites shall be handled by the Competent Authority in conjunction with the relevant authorities.

The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
1. “Unmanned Systems” refer to equipment that operates without personnel onboard and may be operated remotely, autonomously, or by other means in the air, on the surface of water, underwater, on land, or in other environments. Its applications include inspection, transportation, surveillance and reconnaissance, target acquisition, attack, logistics, communications relay, electronic warfare, decoy, mine clearing, mine laying, or other missions.
2. “Dual Use Unmanned Systems” refer to Unmanned Systems based on commercial-specification components that have undergone adaptive modifications to meet the performance requirements of military missions and operational environments.
3. “Military-Civilian Shared Testing Site” refers to a testing site jointly established by the Competent Authority in conjunction with local governments and industry for use by both the military and private-sector entities to conduct flight control, navigation control, and operational simulation testing of Unmanned Systems.
4. “Domestic Content Ratio” refers to the proportion of the output value of Unmanned Systems that originates from domestic enterprises in the course of design, manufacture, assembly, and supply of critical components.
5. “Trusted Supply Chain” refers to a supply chain in which the sourcing, supply and cybersecurity management of Unmanned Systems and their critical components and raw materials comply with the security requirements prescribed by the Competent Authority and with the tiered certification system for Trusted Supply Chain announced by the Competent Authority.
6. “Unmanned Systems Enterprise” refers to an enterprise recognized by the Competent Authority as substantively engaged in the business of Unmanned Systems, and/or their critical components, system integration, software, firmware, data links, cybersecurity, testing and verification, maintenance services, or other critical business activities announced by the Competent Authority, and that meets specified requirements concerning operating revenue, research and development expenditures, technological capabilities, domestic content, or Trusted Supply Chain; the term does not include enterprises whose primary business consists solely of distribution/agency, imports, assembly, resale, or contracting for government projects.
The requirements regarding operating revenue, research and development expenditures, technological capabilities, domestic content, and Trusted Supply Chain applicable to Unmanned Systems Enterprises under Subparagraph 6 of the preceding paragraph shall be prescribed by the Competent Authority.

To establish a long-term and stable mechanism for the development of the Unmanned Systems industry and national defense buildup, to continuously promote the development of the Unmanned Systems industry, strengthen defense self-reliance, build a secure and trusted supply chain system, and enhance international competitiveness, the central government shall, through the annual budget process, budget a total of NT$240 billion over six (6) consecutive years, in principle NT$40 billion per year. Where such amount is insufficient, both the total amount and annual budgets may be increased according to actual needs.

The planning of the Unmanned Systems-based defense architecture shall follow the principle of distributed resilience and avoid concentrated deployment or production.
Unmanned Systems used by public-sector entities shall be capable of transitioning between peacetime and wartime use. Procurement contracts shall comply with the Guidelines for the Procurement of Remote-Controlled Drones and shall expressly prohibit enterprises from Mainland China (including Hong Kong and Macao) from participating in procurement and prohibit individuals from Mainland China (including Hong Kong and Macao) from participating in procurement implementation teams, so as to prevent the infiltration of information and communications products that may endanger national security and to achieve the goal of establishing a fully Trusted Supply Chain in the Republic of China by 2027.

The Competent Authority shall, in accordance with the Unmanned Systems testing-site programs overseen and coordinated by the Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC), accelerate the integration, preparation, and management of testing sites. Within one (1) year after this Act takes effect, the Competent Authority shall, in conjunction with local governments, plan at least three (3) Military-Civilian Shared Testing Sites for the military and private-sector enterprises to conduct flight control, navigation control, anti-jamming, and operational simulation testing of Unmanned Systems, so as to optimize Taiwan’s domestic testing environment and enhance the competitiveness of its Unmanned Systems industry.

The Competent Authority shall annually evaluate the effectiveness of budgets relating to Unmanned Systems. Such evaluation shall include:
1. the effect of Unmanned Systems procurement budgets on the output value of domestic industry;
2. the number and salary levels of technology-related employment opportunities created; and
3. the output value generated from civilian commercial applications and exports.
The evaluation report shall be submitted to the Legislative Yuan for recordation, and the Competent Authority may, upon invitation, attend meetings of the Legislative Yuan to present the report.

An Unmanned Systems Enterprise seeking incentives for domestic content shall obtain Trusted Supply Chain certification established by the Competent Authority.
The Competent Authority shall issue a certificate valid for two (2) years to enterprises that have obtained certification under the preceding paragraph, and shall publish a list of certified enterprises on its official website as a reference for trust assessments by international partners.

Where the amount of a single Unmanned Systems procurement project exceeds NT$100 million, the Competent Authority shall submit a written report to the Legislative Yuan within thirty (30) days after the contract is awarded.

The Executive Yuan shall establish the Special Committee on National Unmanned Systems Industry Development Strategy (the “Special Committee”) to coordinate, promote, and oversee national Unmanned Systems industry policies. The Special Committee shall convene at least once every six (6) months to review the Unmanned Systems Industry Development Framework and major policy matters; extraordinary meetings may be convened in the event of major incidents. The meeting minutes of the Special Committee shall be proactively disclosed on the Executive Yuan’s website and shall include the meeting number, date and time, location, chairperson, attending members, subject matter, agenda, and resolutions.
The Special Committee shall consist of fifteen (15) to nineteen (19) members. One member shall serve as chairperson, a position to be concurrently held by the Vice Premier of the Executive Yuan. The remaining members shall include the heads of the MOEA, the MND, the MOTC, the National Communications Commission (NCC), the Public Construction Commission (PCC) of the Executive Yuan, and the Ministry of Digital Affairs (MODA), as well as scholars and experts selected and appointed by the central authorities from candidates recommended by the respective caucuses of the Legislative Yuan.
The members selected and appointed under the preceding paragraph shall not be less than one-half of the total members of the Special Committee. Their term of office shall be two (2) years, and they may be reappointed upon expiration of their terms. Where a member is replaced during the term for any reason, the replacement member shall serve until the expiration of the original member’s term.
Administrative and staff affairs of the Special Committee shall be handled by the MOEA. The composition, duties, and operating procedures of the Special Committee shall be prescribed by the Executive Yuan.

The Competent Authority shall, in accordance with the Cybersecurity Testing Standards for Remote-Controlled Drones, establish a tiered certification system for Trusted Supply Chain based on the intended use and risk level of Unmanned Systems.
Under the tiered certification system referred to in the preceding paragraph, certification of military Unmanned Systems, military products, and critical components shall be administered by the MND. Certification of commercial, public-service, and other non-military Unmanned Systems shall be administered by the MOEA. The certification system shall be established according to the intended use and risk level of Unmanned Systems and shall, at a minimum, include certification requirements for military products and critical components concerning cybersecurity, Trusted Supply Chains, and national security.
The certification standards, scope of application, verification procedures, and positive lists under the preceding two paragraphs shall be formulated by the central authorities in consultation with relevant agencies and incorporated into the testing mechanism for product families of the same specifications and architecture so as to integrate inspection procedures, avoid duplicative testing, and reduce administrative burden and testing costs, and shall be made publicly available online.

The MOEA shall, in conjunction with relevant agencies, plan the spectrum resources required for Unmanned Systems, as well as the radio frequency resources required for data-link communications, remote identification, and countermeasure testing. Where necessary, mechanisms for allocating experimental and dedicated frequencies may be established.
The MND shall, in conjunction with relevant agencies and based on operational requirements, build satellite communications, data links, dedicated networks, electromagnetic spectrum resources, and other critical communications infrastructure required for military Unmanned Systems to enhance their autonomy, security, anti-jamming capability, and sustained operational capability.

Where Unmanned Systems and their common items have standardized specifications, recurring demand, and are suitable for centralized procurement, the competent procurement authority or an agency designated thereby shall conduct procurement through common supply contracts or other centralized procurement methods in accordance with the Government Procurement Act and applicable provisions governing common supply contracts; the common specifications, safety standards, cybersecurity requirements, Trusted Supply Chain inspection items, and maintenance service terms thereof shall be prescribed by such authority or agency in conjunction with the MOEA and relevant agencies.

The MND shall give priority to procuring, integrating, and training personnel in the use of domestically manufactured, low-cost, and high-performance Unmanned Systems.
In accordance with operational requirements and advances in technology, the MND shall procure attack-type and surveillance-and-reconnaissance-type Unmanned Systems that have an advantage in the sea-crossing and anchorage-landing phases, including the three categories of equipment approved by the Executive Yuan for the Armed Forces: coastal surveillance and reconnaissance unmanned aerial vehicles, coastal attack unmanned aerial vehicles, and small one-way attack unmanned surface vessels.
The MND shall periodically review operational requirements and technological development trends, and shall give priority to promoting the establishment of capabilities for autonomous operation, swarm coordination, anti-jamming navigation, modular design, and rapid mass production.
The MND shall update the certification lists for Trusted Supply Chains and critical components on a monthly basis.

Where any person or enterprise uses critical components, software, firmware, systems, or services that are uncertified, of falsely represented origin, from high-risk sources, or substantively controlled by high-risk sources, and thereby obtains incentives, subsidies, investment, financing, credit guarantees, or eligibility to participate in government procurement under this Act, such eligibility shall be revoked or rescinded, the amounts received shall be recovered, and an administrative fine of not less than one (1) time and not more than three (3) times the amount received shall be imposed.
Any person or enterprise that provides false information during eligibility review, certification, procurement, contract performance, acceptance inspection, subsidy, incentive, investment, financing, or credit guarantee procedures shall be subject to an administrative fine of not less than NT$1 million and not more than NT$5 million.
Any person or enterprise that evades, obstructs, or refuses an audit, testing, random inspection, or retest lawfully conducted by the Competent Authority, a procurement authority, or an entrusted professional institution shall be subject to an administrative fine of not less than NT$500,000 and not more than NT$3 million. Such fines may be imposed repeatedly on a per-violation basis.
Where an act under any of the preceding three paragraphs may give rise to criminal liability, the matter shall be referred to the prosecutorial authorities for investigation.

Within one (1) year after the promulgation and implementation of this Act, the Competent Authority shall, in conjunction with relevant agencies, complete the following:
1. submission of the first Unmanned Systems Industry Development Framework;
2. planning for the safe integration of Unmanned Systems into airspace, maritime, and land management systems; and
3. designation of testing sites, testing corridors, and demonstration zones.
Within six (6) months after the promulgation and implementation of this Act, the Competent Authority shall, in conjunction with relevant agencies, complete the establishment of the tiered certification system of Trusted Supply Chain.

Unmanned Systems Enterprises may, in accordance with the Statute for Industrial Innovation, the Act for Development of Small and Medium Enterprises, the Defense Industry Development Act, the Income Tax Act, and other applicable laws, apply for tax incentives, investment tax credits, income deductions, deferral of income tax, or other incentive or assistance with respect to research and development, equipment investment, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence applications, critical components, testing and verification, talent recruitment, technology contributions as equity, stock-based compensation, financing, credit guarantees, or other matters relating to industrial development.
With respect to the incentives and assistance under the preceding paragraph, the eligible applicants, qualifying expenditures, review criteria, tax credit rates, tax credit periods, annual limits, application procedures, and restrictions on the concurrent application of benefits shall be governed by the respective laws and regulations authorized thereunder.

Where an Unmanned Systems Enterprise has, within the preceding three (3) years, committed a material violation of laws relating to national security, environmental protection, labor, cybersecurity, or aviation safety, as determined by the respective central  authority in charge of the subject industry, it shall not be eligible to apply for the tax incentives under the preceding article, and the tax incentives obtained for the year in which the violation occurred shall cease to apply and shall be recovered.
Where an Unmanned Systems Enterprise is subject to cessation and recovery of tax incentives under the preceding paragraph, the Ministry of Finance shall, after the disposition to cessation or recovery becomes final, publish the name of the Unmanned Systems Enterprise on its website.
The Enforcement Rules of this Act shall be prescribed by the Competent Authority within six (6) months after the promulgation of this Act.
This Act shall take effect six (6) months after its promulgation; provided, however, that Article 4 shall take effect upon promulgation.
